paper: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one (OpenAI, October 6, 2026; OAI:The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026). Sources: preprints/The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/build/{paper.tex, sections/01..15-*.tex, references.tex}; 16 numbered sections (file 12-alternation-imaginary.tex holds Sections 12 and 13). Version note: 'updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection' (previous version Sept 24, 2026). Grade: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (unrefereed, AI-generated, no Lean formalization in the BSD family).

main_theorems.label: Theorem 1.1 (thm:main)
main_theorems.statement: Let E/Q be any elliptic curve with s_2(E) ≤ 1. Then r := rank E(Q) = ord_{s=1} L(E,s) = s_2(E), #Ш(E/Q) < ∞. Moreover, Q_E = L^{(r)}(E,1)(#T_E)^2 / (r! Ω_E Reg_E ∏_{ℓ finite} c_ℓ(E)) ∈ Q_{>0}, v_2(Q_E) = v_2(#Ш(E/Q)). There is no restriction on E[2] or on the reduction of E at two.
main_theorems.hypotheses: s_2(E) := corank_{Z_2} Sel_{2^∞}(E/Q) ≤ 1 (usual local Kummer conditions incl. the real place). Normalizations: Ω_E = ∫_{E(R)}|ω_E| over ALL real components; H = canonical height attached to 2[O] (i.e. twice the usual one), Reg_E = det of B(P,Q) = (H(P+Q)-H(P)-H(Q))/2 on a Z-basis of E(Q)/T_E (Buhler–Gross–Zagier convention); v_2(2)=1. No CM, residual-image, torsion, isogeny or reduction-type hypothesis.

main_theorems.label: Corollary 1.2 (cor:any-prime-bsd, 'An any-prime input criterion')
main_theorems.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve. Suppose that, for some prime p, its full p-power Selmer group with the usual local Kummer conditions at every place satisfies s_p(E) := corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) ≤ 1. Then all conclusions of Theorem 1.1 hold, with common rank r = s_p(E).
main_theorems.hypotheses: s_p(E) ≤ 1 for SOME prime p. Proof (01-introduction.tex:84-95) imports [OpenAIAllPrimeSelmer2026, Theorem 1.1] (rank = s_p and whole Ш finite), then the Kummer sequence at 2 gives s_2 = rank ≤ 1 and Theorem 1.1 applies. Entirely dependent on another OAI manuscript for the odd-p step.

main_theorems.label: Propositions 1.3–1.5 (prop:positive, prop:anchor, prop:cm) — the three comparisons organizing the proof
main_theorems.statement: 1.3 (Positive comparison): Let A/Q be non-CM. If an(A) ≤ 1, then X(A) ≥ 0. Suppose a positive fundamental discriminant a prime to 2N_A, or a=1, satisfies an(A^a) ≤ 1 and X(A^a)=0. Then s_2(A) ≤ 1 implies an(A) = s_2(A) and X(A)=0. 1.4 (Split-pair anchor): Let A/Q be non-CM. There exist a fundamental discriminant h prime to 2N_A, allowing h=1, and an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant k prime to 2hN_A, in which all primes dividing 2hN_A split, such that an(A^h)+an(A^{hk}) = 1, X(A^h)+X(A^{hk}) = 0. 1.5 (CM comparison): If A/Q has CM and s_2(A) ≤ 1, then an(A) = s_2(A) and X(A)=0. Here X(A) = v_2( L^{(an)}(A,1)(#A(Q)_tors)^2 / (an! Ω_A Reg_A ∏c_q(A) #Ш(A/Q)) ) for an(A) ≤ 1.
main_theorems.hypotheses: All three are internal to the Selmer-corank ≤ 1 / analytic-rank ≤ 1 world; X(A) is only defined when an(A) ≤ 1 (uses GZ–Kolyvagin for finiteness of Ш). 1.3 proved in Sections 4–7, 1.4 in Sections 8–10, 12–15 by residual-image cases (reducible / imaginary S_3 / real S_3 / C_3), 1.5 in Section 11.

main_theorems.label: Corollary 16.1 (cor:quadratic-twist-density, 'Exact two-primary BSD for almost all quadratic twists')
main_theorems.statement: Fix E/Q. Among nonzero squarefree d ordered by |d|, the sets {d : s_2(E^d) = j} (j = 0,1) each have density 1/2. For every nonzero squarefree d with s_2(E^d) = j ∈ {0,1}, F = E^d satisfies rank F(Q) = ord_{s=1} L(F,s) = s_2(F) = j, #Ш(F/Q) < ∞, Q_F ∈ Q_{>0}, v_2(Q_F) = v_2(#Ш(F/Q)).
main_theorems.hypotheses: Density statement imported from [OpenAIGoldfeldDensity2026, proof of Theorem 1.2]; pointwise part is Theorem 1.1. 'the formula asserts equality only at the prime two'.

general_results.label: Lemma 2.1 (lem:classical-parity, 'Two-primary parity')
general_results.statement: For every elliptic curve A/Q, (-1)^{s_2(A)} = w(A). For a quadratic field K = Q(√k), s_2(A/K) = s_2(A) + s_2(A^k). Moreover, dim_{F_2} Sel_2(A) − dim_{F_2} A(Q)[2] − s_2(A) is a nonnegative even integer. These statements do not require finiteness of Ш(A).
general_results.hypotheses: None on rank or reduction. Proof imports Kramer81, Kramer–Tunnell82, DD10, DD11, CI16 (dyadic local root numbers), Milne ADT Rem. I.6.11 and Poonen–Stoll Thm 5/Cor 7 (Cassels–Tate alternating), plus a calibrating twist with nonzero central value (FH95) and the rank-zero GZK theorem. Essentially the Dokchitser–Dokchitser/Monsky 2-parity theorem restated.
general_results.relevance: none (2-parity for E/Q is published; seed has s_2(E) ≥ 2, w(E) = +1, consistent).

general_results.label: Theorem 2.2 (thm:classical-gz, 'Split Gross–Zagier formula') and Corollary 2.3 (cor:classical-G, 'full-index discrepancy')
general_results.statement: 2.2: With the preceding hypotheses and units modulo signs one, √D/(8π²(f,f)_N) · L'(f/K,1) = 2 H_{abs,f}(P_X). (GZ-E): L'(E/K,1) = (∫_{E(C)}|ω_E∧ω̄_E| / (√D c_E²)) · 2H_abs(P). 2.3: Under these assumptions [L(E/K,s) simple zero at 1], the single Hilbert-class trace satisfies X(E)+X(E^k) = v_2( [E(K):ZP]² / (c_E² ∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E)² #Ш(E/K)) ).
general_results.hypotheses: f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) newform; K odd fundamental discriminant −D < −4 prime to N with ALL level primes split (Heegner hypothesis); Cor 2.3 additionally assumes ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s) = 1 and uses Tate1966 Thm 2.1 / Cassels65 isogeny invariance for Res_{K/Q}E ~ E×E^k.
general_results.relevance: none for the seed: K = Q(√−7) is NOT a Heegner field for N (3, 2243, 5843 inert) and ord_{s=1} L(E/K,s) ≥ 2.

general_results.label: Lemmas 3.1–3.11 (finite cochain models, complementary duality, line/square switches, global Kummer volume, tame division, pole test)
general_results.statement: 3.1: '…the following constructions can be made by cochain contractions. (1) There are degreewise finite free minimal models with ordinary base change… (2) Suppose on a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter on a sequence of stages the scalar precisions identify… Transfer cochain diagrams at the stages and take matrix limits at all fixed precisions.' 3.4 (strict–finite comparison, eq. D): d(C_F,(Y,Y^∨)) = d(C_*,1) + 2(v(p) + d(U_w,e)). 3.5 (Line switch): d(C_f,Y) = d(C_s,Y'). 3.6 (Square switch): d(C_f,(Y,Y^∨)) = d(C_s,(Y',(Y')^∨)). 3.7 (Kum): for rank one, d(C_Kum,(P,P^∨)) = 2n_P + 2τ_g − s_K with s_K = v_2(#Ш(E/K)).
general_results.hypotheses: Purely cohomological, 2-primary coefficients; 3.7 assumes Ш(E/K) finite and rank one. Relies on an ad hoc 'ultrafilter matrix limit' formalism replacing Iwasawa algebras of moving tame conductors.
general_results.location: sections/03-foundations.tex:223-416 (Lemma 3.1 at 223-256; eq. D at 395-409; switches 451-488; Kum 512-522)
general_results.relevance: none directly; these are p=2 Kolyvagin-system-style finite/singular comparisons (manuscript cites Mazur–Rubin04 §1.2). Not transferable to the lab's odd-p obligations without reproving everything.

general_results.label: Propositions 4.2–4.5 (Kato classes at p=2: integrality, full-level reciprocity, norm relations, period law K4)
general_results.statement: 4.2: 'The classes obtained from (K1) are integral for support containing the primes of 2n_2 and infinity… The projected smoothed classes on Q… admit integral lifts to ordinary positive cohomology.' 4.4: adjoining a fresh prime ℓ ∤ cdn_2L gives the rational norm multiplier 1 − a_ℓ(f)[ℓ]/ℓ + [ℓ]²/ℓ. 4.5 (K4): for the projected weighted class z_ν, the coefficient of its dual exponential relative to ω is ± Δ_ν L^{(M)}(f,ν,1)/Ω_0 · δ_ξ(a), Δ_ν = (c²−cν(c)^{-1})(d²−dν(d)^{-1}).
general_results.hypotheses: Any modular elliptic isogeny class over Q (E' = optimal J_1(N)-quotient modulo cusp differences), square/rectangular level patterns, v_2(M) ≥ 6, c,d prime to 6M (resp. ≡ 1 mod L for 4.5), ν even finite character. Imports Kato04 Thm 9.5 'specialized to k=2, r=r'=1… The theorem applies at p=2', Wang12 distribution formula, Manin–Drinfeld. No rank hypothesis.
general_results.relevance: none: it is the 2-adic Kato Euler system with explicit smoothing; the seed's p=2 obligation (Ш[2^∞]=0) is already settled. Not a statement about odd p.

general_results.label: Proposition 5.1 (prop:positive-determinant:integral, 'Integral positive determinant') with Lemma 5.7
general_results.statement: 5.1: 'The complex C^+ ⊗_B B_{(2)} is a free module of rank two in degree one, up to homotopy. Generically over B, the tensor a∧z is nonzero and gives a coordinate U_raw ∈ Frac B… U = U_raw/Δ · ∏_{q∈S_f, q≠2} D_q/P_q … The assertion is that U ∈ B∖{0}. If the construction is made simultaneously for E' and a positive fundamental twist E'^{(h)}, the two reductions of U differ by a unit of B/2B.' 5.7: 'if an(A_0) = 0, then v_2 U(0) = X(A_0). In particular X(A_0) ≥ 0. If only s_2(A_0)=0 is known and U is a unit, then L(A_0,1) ≠ 0.'
general_results.hypotheses: E' non-CM (Serre open image used for bounded torsion), B = Z_2[[t,u_1,…,u_k]] (cyclotomic + k tame variables at auxiliary primes r_{j,i} → 1), 'Throughout the construction itself, no analytic-rank hypothesis is imposed' (05:9-10). Lemma 5.7 needs an(A_0)=0 or s_2=0.
general_results.relevance: none for the seed obligations: this is an integral 'Kato class ∈ determinant lattice' divisibility (one direction of a 2-adic main conjecture, with tame variables) for non-CM curves at p=2 only; the rank-0 inequality X ≥ 0 is a Kato-type bound on Ш[2^∞]. Seed is done at 2.

general_results.label: Theorem 6.1 (tame:logarithm) and Proposition 6.3 (tame:spectral, 'Spectral-height comparison')
general_results.statement: 6.1: 'Suppose an(E)=1, and let P ∈ E(Q) be nontorsion. Then log_ω z / (log_ω P)² = ± d_0 L'(f,1)/(Ω_0 H(P)). (T1)' 6.3: 'For the horizontal data of Definition 6.2, and the tame height defined below, one has C Ω_0 L(f⊗ε,1) Z'/d_0 = ±(2−a_*) h_λ^K(Q_X,Q_X)/δ. This assertion requires the odd functional sign and the nonzero companion value, but does not assume an(E)=1 or that E(Q) spans the rational Selmer group. In particular, if Q_X is torsion, then Z'=0.'
general_results.hypotheses: E/Q non-CM with primitive form f; 6.1: an(E)=1 (rank one). 6.3: only w(E) = −1 and an auxiliary imaginary quadratic K (odd disc < −4, split at 2N) with L(f⊗ε_K,1) ≠ 0 (FH95); tame characters λ_i of conductor r_i → 1 with Frobenius limit of det 1, trace a_* ≠ ±2. The manuscript says (T1) 'belongs to the framework proposed by Perrin-Riou… Bertolini–Darmon–Venerucci prove such a relation, up to a nonzero rational factor, at odd semistable primes'.
general_results.relevance: none; conceptually adjacent to lemma TH (derivative of a Kato class in a tame direction identified with a tame height of the Heegner trace), but it is cyclotomic-type (even characters of conductor r), 2-adic, and requires w(E) = −1 — the seed E and E^{-7} both have w = +1, and the lab's TH is anticyclotomic at p = 5843.

general_results.label: Lemma 7.5 (lem:positive-completion:bockstein, 'Nonzero Selmer Bockstein') and the unknown-center argument
general_results.statement: 'For the direction of Lemma 7.4, ord_v δ(v) = 1. In particular, C_f^{Sel} is generically acyclic over R = Q_2[[v]].' Used to show: if s_2(E')=1 and the positive anchor hypothesis holds, the dual exponential of the Kato class has a simple zero along the prescribed tame direction, whence by Prop 6.3 L'(E,1) ≠ 0 (07:350-403).
general_results.hypotheses: Non-CM, s_2(E')=1, positive anchor hypothesis (unit U) — i.e. corank-one only. The Bockstein nonvanishing itself uses only a nonzero compact Selmer class x, its self-cup primitive k (Lemma 7.3, via Poitou–Tate and local Kummer isotropy) and a Frobenius direction with k(g) − β(g)g_T(g_T−1)^{-1}x(g) ≠ 0.
general_results.relevance: none (corank ≤ 1 only; K-RANK2). Note: this is the manuscript's 2-adic 'Selmer corank 1 ⇒ analytic rank 1' step for arbitrary non-CM curves — far beyond published p-converse theorems; extraordinary claim.

general_results.label: Proposition 8.1 (split-measures:reducible-input, 'Reducible split-product comparison') and Propositions 9.11–9.12
general_results.statement: 8.1: 'Let E/Q be a non-CM elliptic curve with E(Q)[2] ≠ 0, and put N = cond(E). Let d ≡ 7 (mod 16) be prime and suppose that every prime dividing 2N splits in K = Q(√−d). If s_2(E/K)=1, then L(E/K,s) = L(E,s)L(E^{-d},s) has a simple zero at 1, and X(E)+X(E^{-d}) = 0. If the product is already known to have a simple zero at 1, the same valuation identity holds without separately assuming the Selmer corank condition.' 9.12 (eq. E): 2(n_P+τ_g) = 2v_2(c_E) + 2Σ_ℓ v_2(c_ℓ) + s_K.
general_results.hypotheses: Non-CM, rational 2-torsion, d ≡ 7 mod 16 prime, all primes of 2N split in K, s_2(E/K) = 1 (or simple zero of L(E/K,s)). Proof: paired 2-adic CM-disk logarithmic measures (BDP-style depleted primitives) vs strict Selmer determinant over Z_2[[t,u]], unit comparison via residual Eisenstein congruence.
general_results.relevance: none. Seed check: E(Q)[2] = Z/2 ✓, d = 7 ≡ 7 mod 16 prime ✓, but 3, 2243, 5843 are inert in Q(√−7) ✗ and s_2(E/K) = s_2(E) + s_2(E^{-7}) ≥ 2 ✗.

general_results.label: Proposition 9.7 (split-local:derivative, 'Inert derivative identity', eq. K) with Lemma 9.5
general_results.statement: 'Fix a finite collection of auxiliary inert prime sequences satisfying the full-Tate approximation conditions… Let Z_I be their descended, χ-weighted corestrictions to K, transferred to the limiting coefficient model. In the finite and singular coordinates f_loc, s_loc of Lemma 9.5, at a newly switched prime ℓ ∉ I one has s_loc(Z_{I∪{ℓ}}) = J f_loc(Z_I), f_loc(Z_{I∪{ℓ}}) = 0, (K) and the transverse condition in the second identity holds at every switched prime.'
general_results.hypotheses: Modular abelian variety A (or E), K imaginary quadratic with O_K^× = {±1}, 2 and the level split; auxiliary inert primes ℓ_i → −1, a_ℓ → 0, ρ(γ_i) → J with J² = 1 (2-adically, on the full Tate module). Descent multiplier L via Bogomolov80 homotheties. No rank hypothesis.
general_results.relevance: none: a 2-adic Kolyvagin-derivative (finite/singular) relation for Heegner points at inert primes; the lab's level-raising/bipartite route (TH) is at p = 5843.

general_results.label: Proposition 9.13 (split-local:heegner-rank, 'Characteristic-zero Heegner rank test', eq. K0)
general_results.statement: 'Let f be a normalized primitive weight-two newform of trivial nebentypus and level N_f, and let A be its modular abelian factor. Let K have odd fundamental discriminant −D < −4, prime to N_f, and suppose every prime dividing N_f splits in K… Assume V_f|_{G_K} absolutely irreducible. Then L(f/K,s) has a simple zero at 1 ⟹ H^1_f(K,V_f) = F_f y, y ≠ 0, τy = −w(f)y, where y is the Kummer class of the projected Hilbert trace… For a general A, no assertion of finiteness for its entire prime-primary Tate–Shafarevich group is included.'
general_results.hypotheses: Heegner hypothesis for K, V_f|G_K absolutely irreducible, L(f/K,s) simple zero; coefficient field F_f ⊃ Q_2 (2-adic). Proof: GZ86/CST14 + inert derivative identity (K) + global reciprocity; 'does not require a residual Euler-system bound' (Remark 9.14).
general_results.relevance: none (Kolyvagin's rank-one theorem re-proved 2-adically; seed has ord ≥ 2 over any K).

general_results.label: Proposition 10.1 (prop:reducible-seed, 'Finite Selmer seed'), Proposition 10.8 (split imaginary partner), Lemma 13.3, Lemma 14.3, Lemma 15.1 (twisting to small 2-Selmer)
general_results.statement: 10.1: 'There are a permitted twisting factor h and an elliptic curve E_0, isogenous over Q to E^h, with rational two-torsion and dim Sel_2(E_0) = dim E_0(Q)[2]. (seed)' 10.8: 'For h, E_0 in Proposition 10.1, there is a fresh prime d ≡ 7 (mod 16) such that K = Q(√−d) splits all primes of 2hN_E, and d_2(E_0^{-d}) = s_2(E_0^{-d}) = 1, s_2(E_0) = 0, s_2(E_0/K) = 1.' 13.3: for S_3-imaginary image there is a squarefree h of primes ≡ 1 mod 8 with dim Sel_2(E^h) + dim Sel_2(E^{hk}) = 1 and s_2(E^h/K)=1.
general_results.hypotheses: E non-CM with rational 2-torsion (10.1/10.8) or residual image S_3/C_3 (13.3, 14.3, 15.1); twisting primes avoid 2N_E; 'Neither construction uses analytic nonvanishing or finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group.' Finite 2-descent + Chebotarev (Mazur–Rubin10 Lemma 3.2/Prop 3.3/Lemma 3.5 style), plus an 'orientation by isogeny' Lemma 10.5 maximizing v_2(Ω∏c_q) in the 2-isogeny graph.
general_results.relevance: none: produces auxiliary twists of small 2-Selmer rank; says nothing about E itself.

general_results.label: Theorem 11.3 (cm:external-units, 'Individual-character elliptic-unit comparison') and Lemma 11.4
general_results.statement: 'Let Γ ≅ Z_2² be the free pro-2 factor of the ray-tower group… If f_χ | f, then, inside generic rank-one cohomology, Λ_O z_{2^∞ f} = det^{-1}_{Λ_O} RΓ(O_L[1/2f], Λ(χ)(1)). For the character motive of type (1,0)… elliptic-unit reciprocity gives the period equation per(exp^* z(γ)) = L_{2f}(φ̄,1)γ… The equation includes the case of a zero L-value.' 11.4 (C2): under concentration, O z(T_α ψ) = D(RΓ(O_L[1/2f], T_α ψ)), 'No nonvanishing hypothesis on a complex L-value is required.'
general_results.hypotheses: L imaginary quadratic, CM Hecke character of type (1,0), p = 2. 'The determinant assertion is the Johnson-Leung–Kings theorem in the form of [BF23, Theorem 4.1]… That theorem includes p=2. The period equation is Kato's reciprocity law [Kato04, Prop 15.9], in the CM formulation [BF23, Prop 3.1].'

general_results.label: Proposition 11.14 (cm:corank-one, 'CM corank one') and Corollary 11.11 (CM corank zero)
general_results.statement: 11.14: 'If E/Q is CM and s_2(E) = 1, then an(E) = 1 and X(E) = 0.' 11.11: 'If E/Q is CM and s_2(E) = 0, then an(E) = 0 and X(E) = 0.'
general_results.hypotheses: E/Q CM, s_2(E) ≤ 1. 11.14 claims a 2-adic CM corank-one converse at EVERY reduction type at 2 (published: LTYZ2025/BCST22 need good ordinary at 2).

general_results.label: Lemma 12.1 (alternation-imaginary:alternation, 'Conjugate Bockstein alternation') and Corollary 12.2 (parity of special and generic ranks)
general_results.statement: 12.1: 'With the coefficient module, local conditions, and isotropy data just specified, let s ∈ R be a regular scalar. On degree one for coefficients mod s, with ∂ the Bockstein from mod s², one has ⟨x, ∂x⟩ = 0. (H1)' 12.2: 'For a perfect two-term DVR complex in degrees 1,2 with perfect self-duality of shift −3, arising from the preceding local conditions and satisfying (H1), the generic and special first-cohomology dimensions have the same parity.'
general_results.hypotheses: V = Ind_K^Q(Tχ), T a free plane from Q with perfect alternating form, χ anticyclotomic, R a complete 2-adic scalar/power-series ring; local conditions: one unrestricted coordinate at split pairs, unramified at discriminant primes. No rank hypothesis.
general_results.relevance: none directly: an anticyclotomic Selmer-parity lemma (Nekovář/Howard-type) at p = 2. The lab's anticyclotomic route is at p = 5843 and uses published BD/BLV; no p-independent statement is given.

general_results.label: Proposition 14.4 (real:detector, 'The detector at infinity') and Lemma 14.6 (parity on primitive components)
general_results.statement: 14.4: 'There is an F_2-linear functional Θ: H^1(⟨σ⟩, T_2J) → F_2, Θ T_p = tr W(Fr_p) Θ (p ∤ 2n), Θ([Y']) ≠ 0. (R0)' 14.6: 'If g is one of the primitive components or its quadratic twist and has odd functional sign, its two-adic characteristic-zero Kummer Selmer dimension over Q at the chosen embedding is odd.'
general_results.hypotheses: W = E[2] with image S_3 and REAL quadratic subfield L; J = J_0(n) with n = 2^δ d_L^odd (b^odd ℓ_0)², σ = w_n c; Y' = (T_ℓ − ℓ − 1)·(Hilbert trace) for a Heegner K of discriminant −d ≡ 7 mod 8 splitting 2nhN_E.
general_results.relevance: none (residual real-S_3 branch of the 2-adic anchor).

general_results.label: Lemma 14.9/14.11/14.12 (Pfaffian cofactor lift and 'Pfaffian divisibility with repeated factors')
general_results.statement: 14.11: 'Let R_0 be a commutative ring, let A, B be alternating matrices of even size, and let Δ = diag(d_1,…,d_{2r}). Suppose A = ΔBΔ, v = Δb, L = HΔ with all matrices integral… If Q_Δ = ∏_k d_k, then Pf(A) = Q_Δ Pf(B), L#A v = Q_Δ H #B b. Thus L#A v + Pf(A)c is divisible by Q_Δ for every integral c. Neither regularity nor coprimality of the d_k is required.' 14.12: global coordinates of the cofactor-lifted cycle are divisible by Q_aux = ∏_{j>0} α_j.
general_results.hypotheses: Pure algebra (14.11); 14.12 in the real-S_3 strict-pair setting over R_1 = A[[u_0]].

general_results.label: Proposition 15.4 (cyclic:ray-basis, 'Primitive ray determinant') and Proposition 15.6 (comparator determinant, Y2)
general_results.statement: 15.4: 'The class z_S = e_S z_ray is a basis of the inverse determinant of the unrestricted global complex on O(τ)(1)τ, with support S', over the dyadic character integers. Rationally this determinant is its single H^1-line.' 15.6: v_2(D) = 2v_2(ℓ_w z_ray) + Σ_{q∈S, v_0|q} v_2(P_q(χ(Fr_{v_0}))).
general_results.hypotheses: K imaginary quadratic with O_K^× = ±1 and odd class number, τ = ρχ a ray-class character of order 3·2^a (ρ cubic from the C_3 residual image), z_ray the weighted Kummer trace of a Siegel unit (Oukhaba03 §2.2 normalization), S' ≠ ∅; proof via S'-truncated Dedekind class number formula and Epstein–Kronecker limit formula.
general_results.relevance: none (a one-character Stark/Rubin-type unit determinant at p=2 used as an Eisenstein comparator).

general_results.label: Lemma 11.6 (cm:log-nonzero) and Lemma 8.5/8.6/8.7 (integral depleted primitive, disk measure support, exact logarithmic primitive M1)
general_results.statement: 11.6: 'For every nontorsion P ∈ B(Q), one has log_ω P ≠ 0' (B a Q-simple CM abelian variety, via Fuchs–Pham p-adic analytic subgroup theorem). 8.5: F_0 = d_mod^{-1} f^{[2]} converges to an integral weight-zero function on the ordinary locus, including when 2 | N. 8.7: 'F_0 = P_2(V_2) G (M1)' on interior ordinary CM disks; 8.6: the disk measure μ with F(z) = ∫ z^x dμ(x) is supported on Z_2^×.
general_results.hypotheses: Primitive weight-two newform of trivial character, imaginary quadratic field with units ±1 split at 2 and the level; ordinary (split) CM disks. No rank hypothesis.
general_results.relevance: none: 2-adic BDP-type anticyclotomic measure construction (manuscript: 'antecedents in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna §3.8, 5.3'); the seed's split-at-p anticyclotomic route needs p = 5843 (inert in K = Q(√−7), so even the analogue would not apply).

applicability.seed_E: NOT APPLICABLE (kill test K-RANK2). Theorem 1.1 needs s_2(E) ≤ 1; the seed has rank E(Q) = 2, so s_2(E) ≥ 2 (and s_p(E) ≥ 2 for every p, so Corollary 1.2 also fails). The manuscript itself states it 'makes no assertion about higher Selmer corank or the remaining prime parts' (01:18-20). Every intermediate comparison (Props 1.3–1.5, 8.1, 9.11–9.13, 11.14, 13.1, 14.1, 15.9) is conditioned on Selmer corank ≤ 1 over Q or over an auxiliary split K, or on a simple zero. The only rank-free statements (Lemma 2.1 parity; Props 4.2–4.5 Kato classes; Prop 5.1 integral determinant; Prop 6.3 spectral-height, which needs w = −1; Prop 9.7 derivative identity; Lemma 12.1 alternation; twisting Props 10.1/10.8) are all 2-adic, and the seed's p = 2 obligation (Ш[2^∞] = 0) is already PROVED in the lab. Contribution to FIN: none. ORDER9: none (needs Ш[p^∞]=0 for p ≥ 5). Q36: none — no rank-2 archimedean (Gross–Zagier-type) formula appears; the manuscript's leading-term identities are rank ≤ 1 only and at the prime 2 only.
applicability.twist_Em7: FORMALLY APPLICABLE at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT. E^{-7} has rank 0 and L(E^{-7},1) ≠ 0 (PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED), hence by GZK Ш(E^{-7}) is finite and s_2(E^{-7}) = 0 ≤ 1; Theorem 1.1 allows additive reduction at 2 (I_1^*) and rational 2-torsion. Its new content for E^{-7} is only v_2( L(E^{-7},1)·(#T)^2 / (Ω_{E^{-7}} ∏ c_ℓ(E^{-7})) ) = v_2(#Ш(E^{-7}/Q)) (rank 0 and finiteness are classical). This touches the '#Ш(E^{-7}/Q)' item only at p = 2 and gives nothing about odd parts of #Ш(E^{-7}). Cost reduction: nil — Ш(E^{-7})[2] is obtainable by a cheap 2-descent, whereas verifying this 9,500-line manuscript (ultrafilter finite models, Pfaffian lifts, 2-adic CM measures) is far costlier. The published literature (Zhao 1997, CLZ 2020, Shu–Zhai 2021, Kriz–Li 2019) does not cover E^{-7} generically, so if the manuscript were correct it would be the only route to the 2-part of BSD for E^{-7}; but this is not a seed obligation. Nothing for E^{-7} at p ∈ {3, 2243, 4547, 5843} or good primes.
applicability.by_prime: p = 2: this is the manuscript's only prime; its general lemmas' hypotheses (any E[2], any reduction at 2, non-CM via Serre) are satisfied by the seed, but the seed's 2-primary obligation is already settled and Theorem 1.1 fails for E (s_2 ≥ 2); for E^{-7} see above. p = 3: nothing — 3 appears only as a smoothing-avoidance prime ('c,d prime to 6'); the seed's 3-part is already done. p = 2243 (split mult.), p = 5843 (nonsplit mult.), p = 4547 (additive, pot. supersingular): nothing; no odd-p Iwasawa, Kolyvagin, level-raising, or additive-prime statement is made; Corollary 1.2 would require s_p(E) ≤ 1, which fails. Good ordinary / good supersingular p ≥ 5: nothing; the manuscript's odd-prime inputs enter only as local Euler factors P_q and Tamagawa/Haar identities. Lemma TH (anticyclotomic theta-element derivative at p = 5843, K = Q(√−7) with 5843 inert): no bearing — the closest analogue (Prop 6.3 / Lemma 7.5) is 2-adic, cyclotomic-tame, and requires w(E) = −1.

red_flags: Extraordinary claim with no residual hypothesis: Theorem 1.1 asserts a 2-adic Selmer-corank-one ⇒ analytic-rank-one converse for ALL non-CM curves (Section 7.2–7.4, via a nonzero Selmer Bockstein and the 'torsion implication' of Prop 6.3), and CM corank-one converse at every reduction type at 2 (Prop 11.14), far beyond published p-converse theorems (which need p odd and residual/local hypotheses, or good ordinary at 2 for CM). Treat the unknown-center argument as the highest-risk step.

Every determinant/measure comparison in Sections 5–15 rests on this.

notes: Read in full: paper.tex, sections 01–15 (9,525 lines incl. references.tex), both READMEs of the internal dependencies, history.md, CONTENTS.md, and the relevant intro/reduction passages of the two companions. Summary verdict for the lab: the manuscript is a 2-adic, Selmer-corank-≤1 result; by kill test K-RANK2 it cannot apply to the seed curve E (rank 2), and its only applicable instance, Theorem 1.1 for E^{-7} (s_2 = 0), yields the 2-part of #Ш(E^{-7}) — not a seed obligation, cheaper by direct 2-descent, and only at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT. No statement addresses odd primes, additive/multiplicative primes, anticyclotomic theta elements at inert p, rank-2 leading terms, or any computational shortcut; nothing here reduces the cost of the lab's Kurihara, B.18, Brandt or plectic computations. Should the lab ever want the 2-part of BSD for a rank-0 twist, the chain to verify would be: Sections 2–7 (positive comparison) + Section 10 (reducible anchor, since E^{-7} has rational 2-torsion) + Sections 8–9 (split comparison) + Section 16, i.e. roughly 5,000 lines, plus the Kato-at-p=2 and nonvanishing-with-local-conditions imports.
